In a world not unlike our own, but marred by the unnatural, there existed figures of legend, whispered about in hushed tones and viewed with a wary eye by the common folk. Among these was the figure known only as Simon, a man with no known source of income, no job, no usual place of residence, and no face familiar to those who traveled the less traveled paths of the city more accustomed to the shadows.

It was said that Simon could see things that others could not. Not in the straightforward manner of a seeing auras or mirrors or the like, but a sight of a different kind, one woven from the fabric of the ineffable truths that moved and reshaped the very core of reality itself. If he looked hard enough, Simon was thought to see into an unfathomable knowledge of the past and future that left most who considered it skeptical, thinking of it as a wild and unfounded superstition.

Simon lived, as had been his wont for years, in an apartment with no address, a space so hidden deep in the heart of the city that it was a wonder anyone could find it at all. Its doorways were hidden in alleyways between buildings, light never rayed to them in daylight, and even at night it was often brushed by the passersby and largely forgotten.

One evening, as autumn colors painted the sky, Simon emerged from his apartment wearing his usual impeccably clean clothes, even if, to many, they seemed a little strange, as if they were ill-suited to the world outside. He walked, or, rather, floated - something that seemed entirely natural to him - down to the edge of the city he so often found himself actively avoiding.

It was here that he found his rare opportunity, the first that he had seen for what seemed like a lifetime. An artifact, a lock of hair from a marquis long forgotten, erred from a nearby church's archives, a whisper of a story that had been lost to time itself.

Simon's eyes, which always possessed an unsettling glow, shone bright as he reached out, fingers trembling slightly, to touch the lock of hair. In an instant, not just his body, but everything around him, shifted. The colors of the world changed, not so much that they became impossible to recognize, but as if they had been saturated by an unknown light.

At the farthest edge of this change was the present city, a teetering edifice of stone, steel, and glass, all of it suddenly frail and off kilter. Simon stared in disbelief, a trinket in hand, as history slipped through his fingers like sand.

His sight had revealed that the city, all city, was only a minor artifact in a grand design, a moment in the endless cycle of existence, and Simon, fragile, worn, and unexplained, held the key to all that followed, the lock that could change the course of history itself.

With that knowledge grasped, and tugging at his very consciousness like a force unseen, Simon took another step away from the reality of the present, retreating further into the murky waters of his vision. There, in a world not unlike his own, but with abnormalities and omens twisting reality, he found the origin of the lock of hair. A legend of old, linked to a mystery that had hinted at the Future rather than just foretell it, and whose hand had changed the course of the city, and every city, to come.

In that first light, the city was but a fleeting color, one fading from view, replaced by a beauty so strange and unfamiliar it reeled even Simon, all too real and too aware, into a search more ancient yet than any city, or mythos, left lying in forgotten archives. The future, no longer vague and unknowable, hurtled towards him, riding the winds and rivers and the very bones of the Earth itself.

And with that knowledge, Simon took his first step into the unknown, a man who, when known at all, was a blur, or a whisper, a dream or a ghost, and who no longer was bound by the future lurked beneath the surface. Instead, he found himself a shade, a herald, unlikeliest of all among legends and mysteries, armed not with weapons or wisdom but with the truth, an active and ongoing killjoy to the history breeding closed loop.

And, at the heart of the City, or cities, or continuities, Simon awaited. His fate limitless, his purpose encoded in the very making of time itself. As the city perished, he arose, transformed in the heat of the sun to timeless, shape-shifting, and celestial Simon of the faint light of his first glimpse of Infinity.
